subject: Consumption Stabilizer — commercial appendix and billing ops playbook
messages:
From: Sabrina Lee <sabrina.lee@novamed.com>

Subject: RFP commercial: consumption variability / surge handling — clarifications requested

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Thank you for the commercial section you submitted with the RFP. The procurement team reviewed and has a handful of follow-ups to better understand how Redwood would handle month-to-month variability and one-off surges. Specifically: 

- We need a concise description of any pricing smoothing you offer (true-up cadence, amortization windows, notification thresholds).
- How are pre-purchased burst credits handled on invoices and in reporting? Are they refundable or amortized?
- If we commit to an annual token volume but usage spikes above the committed band, what caps or mitigations are available to avoid extreme invoice volatility?
- Can you provide explicit overage math (examples with 10%, 50%, and 200% monthly spikes) and the resulting invoice impacts?
- Any SLA credit or commercial protection offered when a regional outage forces reroute to a higher-cost region?

Procurement would like this content back as language we can include in the RFP appendix by COB next Friday. I attached the commercial questionnaire (short form) — please reference question numbers in your reply so we can map back. Also copying procurement for timing.

Thanks,
Sabrina Lee

NovaMed Health Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: RFP commercial: consumption variability — internal draft response

Team —

Drafting a concise appendix for NovaMed. Key principles I want to align on before I send Sabrina a formal response: keep their procurement comfortable with predictable spend while protecting Redwood economics and encouraging a modest commit. Proposed approach below — please flag if any number is a non-starter. I attached a working pricing model (stabilizer_pricing_model.xlsx).

Summary proposal (short):
- Commit structure: Annual committed token volume with monthly invoicing and monthly true-up. Customer picks an annual commit band (monthly target = annual / 12).
- Smoothing window: We offer a 3-month rolling smoothing mechanism. Usage above the monthly target is billed as overage immediately at the applicable overage rate, but invoiced over the subsequent 3 months (amortized) at 1/3 per month if customer opts into \"consumption stabilizer\". This reduces invoice spikes while preserving near-term cost signals.
- Burst credits: Option to purchase pre-paid burst credits (one-time SKU) at a discounted unit price. Pre-paid credits are amortized monthly across the billing period but are non-refundable. Unused credits are eligible to be rolled into the next 3 months once per year (not retroactively refundable).
- Overage caps: For committed customers we cap monthly overage exposure to 2x the standard overage unit price per token; additionally, for any single calendar month where usage > 300% of monthly target, we will automatically convert the excess to a temporary burst bucket priced at 1.8x unit rate and trigger a required engagement with our CS to assess workload optimization.
- Discounting: Standard list unit price (per 1K input+output tokens). Annual prepaid commit gets 20% off list on committed volume. 12-month committed billing with monthly true-up. 36-month contracts eligible for an additional 5% strategic discount (sales approval).
- SLA/regional-failover protection: If a Redwood region outage forces reroute that increases per-token cost (e.g., to a more expensive region or advanced variant), Redwood provides a one-time \"stability credit\" equal to 25% of the incremental cost for the affected billing period, applied as an invoice credit. No SLA credit for customer-side misconfiguration.

Examples to include in the appendix (will add numeric tables in the spreadsheet):
- 10% monthly spike: fully absorbed by existing smoothing, nominal amortized over 3 months; additional invoice delta small (~+2-5%).
- 50% monthly spike: overage billed then amortized -> shows ~+15-22% across 3-month window.
- 200% monthly spike: triggers burst bucket pricing at 1.8x for the delta above 300% threshold; immediate notification and CS engagement; invoice impact capped by amortization and explicit cap.

Open items I need from you:
1) Ben — confirm the pre-paid credit amortization language and whether we want a partial refund clause for terminated contracts (I recommend no refunds; credits convert to account balance for 12 months).
2) Karthik — can you draft the RFP-friendly legal-lite paragraph we send to procurement (two short bullet points) so we keep it concise?
3) Laura — confirm that the 25% regional-failover credit and the 1.8x burst pricing are acceptable commercially (and if not propose alternate percentiles).

Plan: incorporate your edits today, send an external reply to Sabrina by EOD PT tomorrow with spreadsheet examples and SOW insert language.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick thoughts, happy with the framework. Two small asks: 

- Pre-paid burst credits: change wording to \"non-refundable except in the event of contract termination within 30 days of purchase, where a pro-rata refund may be issued at Redwood's discretion.\" That gives procurement a small safety valve.
- Stability credit: rather than a flat 25% incremental-cost credit, propose a tiered scale: 25% credit for first incident in a 12-month period, 35% if two incidents occur, and a customer-level review for repeated outages. Keeps incentives aligned for larger customers.

Also — recommend we include a short example invoice line item format in the appendix so procurement's accounting team can map fields: Commit unit, actual usage, amortized overage, burst credits applied, stability credits applied. I added a tab in the spreadsheet.

Ben

Thanks — I took Ben's inputs and wrote two short, RFP-friendly bullets for procurement. Paste below; feel free to shorten. I'll attach a one-page commercial appendix and a draft SOW snippet (SOW-draft-v1.docx) to the external reply.

Proposed RFP appendix language (legal-lite):
1) Consumption Stabilizer: Customer selects an annual committed token volume. Monthly true-ups reconcile actual usage against the committed band. Customer may opt into a 3-month amortization for overages (the \"Consumption Stabilizer\") which spreads the invoiced overage evenly across the subsequent three invoices; pre-paid burst credits are amortized monthly and are non-refundable except as described in Section 2.

2) Overages, Burst, and Stability Protections: Overages are billed at the applicable overage rate per 1,000 tokens. For single-month usage that exceeds 300% of the monthly committed target, excess consumption will be moved to a temporary burst bucket priced at 1.8x the standard overage rate; for committed customers, monthly financial exposure is capped at 2x the standard overage rate. In the event of a Redwood infrastructure-related regional failover that increases per-token cost, Redwood will apply a stability credit equal to 25% of the incremental cost for the affected billing period; credits escalate with repeat incidents per the commercial appendix.

Pricing table (inline example):
- List unit price: $0.020 per 1K tokens
- Annual commit (example band): 120M tokens/year => $19,200/month list price before discount
- Annual commit discount: 20% => $0.016 per 1K tokens applied to committed volume
- Overage rate (standard): $0.025 per 1K tokens
- Burst bucket rate (above 300% threshold): $0.045 per 1K tokens (1.8x)
- Overage cap: Maximum invoice exposure from overage for committed accounts limited to 2x the standard overage rate per token within a month

I added a short clause for invoice format and reporting cadence. We'll link to the spreadsheet in the external reply so procurement sees the worked examples.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference
